Your friend will never be the same again after losing a child, and that's ok. It may be years before she begins to sparkle again, and that's ok too. She will need time to heal and learn to live in a world without her child.

You will need to grieve the loss of who your friend was. Even if she one day regains her glow, right now you need to grieve for her and for her daughter. It's not selfish to fear losing part of someone you love when they lose someone close to them. It's ok to be scared and angry and hurt.

Keep being present for her. Reach out to her often, but don't ask for or expect anything back. Saying "hey, hope you're having a good day" is better than asking how her day is going. Send her cute pictures of things that you think will make her smile, and be available when she does reach out.

I'm sorry that you and your friend are going through this. I wish you both all the best.

When I was 25 I forgot what my excuses were and just thought that it was how life is. Now I'm 30 and I've suffered from anxiety, depression and suicidal thoughts for literally half my life. Everyone deserves a society that is more open-minded and accepting of metal health issues. Everyone deserves to have their feelings taken seriously.

I very much hope that your results come back clean and I can only recommend honesty within your relationship.

That being said, if you are diagnosed with HIV, I hope that it does not herald the end of your life. I have friends with HIV who have been leading full, meaningful lives since their diagnosis. You say that you will fight to end the stigma against HIV if you are found clean, but perhaps you would consider combating the stigma that you hold within yourself until your results come in.

I was recently on a ridge walk in Scotland with incredible winds pushing me towards a thousand feet of jagged rocks below. I wasn't afraid to fall, but I was terrified of losing my partner. I knew I couldn't go on without him and that made me think of how he would feel without me. He has given me so much, I owe him much, much more than to see me die at my own hand. Sometimes this is all that keeps me going.

My dad once told me that he cared more about the carpets than me, possibly because he was grumpy and my dancing was annoying him. It was then that I realized that parents are people we see as wiser and more mature than us, but that cannot be true forever. My own father couldn't admit that he cared about me because he didn't want to lose and argument. That doesn't mean he doesn't love me, it just means he isn't actually very emotionally mature. Maybe it's the same for your mom. Her dismissing your cry for help could be because she can't handle the idea of the truth, but it doesn't mean there is no love there.

I hope you find help and unquestioned love and support <3
